chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim and Al-Fadl, two sons of Yazeed Al-Ashari, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The closest state a servant can reach to disbelief is that he establishes brotherhood with a man upon the Religion, yet he counts his slips and mistakes against him in order to rebuke him with them one day.
ai.seo_question: What is the closest state to disbelief in social relationships according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often cited to illustrate how minor social friction can escalate into major theological deviation, emphasizing that the intent behind observing others' faults matters more than the faults themselves. The chain of narration (isnad) traces back to the Imams al-Sadiq and al-Baqir, underscoring the authority of this warning within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining humility and avoiding the 'tallier of slips' mentality that breeds arrogance and eventual kufr.
